headline: Brazil's president trails his predecessor's son and faces a run-off
headline_short: Brazil's election goes to a run-off
deck: The former president's son took 47.1 per cent to the president's 45.1; the two meet again on 25 October.
standard: Flávio Bolsonaro, a right-wing senator for the state of Rio de Janeiro, won the first round of Brazil's presidential election on Sunday with 47.1 per cent of the vote. Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, the left-wing president, took 45.1 per cent. As neither won more than 50 per cent, the two meet in a run-off on 25 October.

Lula, 80, called the result 'unexpected'; he had been convinced he would win in the first round. Bolsonaro, 45, is the son of Jair Bolsonaro, the former president Lula beat four years ago. His father is serving 27 years in prison for a failed coup attempt after the 2022 election.
short: Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro, won the first round of Brazil's presidential election on Sunday with 47.1 per cent, ahead of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, the president, on 45.1 per cent. The two meet in a run-off on 25 October.
